name: Location button (one time share)
plain: A system button the person taps to share location once, with no prompt or settings.
meaning: App gets one time precise location without long term permission.

android.permission: None; Jetpack LocationButton (Beta 3, March 2026), ship status not confirmed
android.note: Preview; Android 17 stable ship not confirmed here

ios.permission: None; CLLocationButton gives one time authorization
ios.note: Does not require Info.plist usage string for the one time use

limits.headline: Can get your location once when you tap the Share button, with no prompt
limits.user_action: You tap the system Share Location button
can: Get your location one time for this tap
Use that spot to find nearby places or fill an address
Do it with no permission prompt or settings trip on iPhone
cannot: Follow you after the single tap
Use the one time spot in the background
Work on Android until the button ships; it is still in preview there
Use the spot again later without another tap
limits.differs: iPhone has the button now. Android's button is in preview and not confirmed to ship.

story.what_it_is: A system button you tap to share your location one time, with no prompt and no settings.

marketing.name: Location Button
marketing.pitch: A system button that gives an app one time access to your location, with no permission prompt needed.

story.for_you: You see a blue Share Current Location button inside the app. You tap it and the app gets your spot once. There is no long permission step and the app does not keep it.
story.for_makers: Makers get a quick, trusted way to get a location for one task without scaring users. It works well for store finders and one off searches. It cannot track you, so apps that need continuous tracking still need a permission.

use_cases.example: A store app has a Find stores near me button that fills your location once for the search.
A restaurant app uses the button to fill your delivery address on first order.
A taxi app uses one tap to set your pickup point.
A hotel app asks for your spot to show nearby rooms for tonight.
A parking app uses the button to find a spot close by without ongoing access.
A meetup app lets you tag where you are in a post once.

story.android_note: Android has no exact twin. It offers a one time option in the permission dialog instead.
story.ios_note: This is an iPhone feature in the CoreLocationUI framework, and the button gives a temporary Allow While Using the App.

technical_bounds: System draws button so apps cannot spoof
